title: Unbounded message history growth in memory
reasoning: The Chat component appends every message to the messages state array without any cap. While useChatHistory limits the initial preload to 60 messages, subsequent user interactions grow the array indefinitely. A long session (e.g., 200+ exchanges) will cause performance degradation due to re-renders of the entire message list and memory bloat. The historySnapshot sent to the API also grows unbounded, potentially exceeding API token limits or backend payload limits.
reproduction:
1. Start a chat session
2. Send 100+ messages
3. Observe increasing render time and memory usage in DevTools
4. API request payload grows linearly with message count
recommendation: Implement a sliding window for in-memory messages (e.g., keep only the last 50 exchanges). When sending to the API, slice historySnapshot to the most recent N messages to fit context windows. Persist the full history server-side (already done via persist()), but only render/process a window client-side.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included. Performance degradation requires stress testing with many messages, which is beyond typical unit test scope.
suggestedRegressionTest: Simulate 100 message exchanges and assert that messages.length does not exceed a defined cap (e.g., 60).
minimumFixScope: src/src/portal/Chat.tsx send function: slice historySnapshot and cap messages array
